page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Lemon-sized luxury boxes
title: Lemon-sized luxury boxes
description:
Anna continues to sort out the order of Imperial Lemons for Mr Lime. He gives her a call, this time to discuss business. He wants some luxury boxes to put the lemons in and Anna needs to find them if she wants to keep her client happy. When she does she has to email Mr Lime but what should she say?
This episode focuses on placing an order.
phrases: I'd like to place an order for...
When can we expect to receive them?

listening_challenge.question: What colour are the Imperial lemon-sized luxury boxes?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Welcome to the offices of Tip Top Trading...
(ongoing sound of annoying mobile phone ringtone)

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Anna, are you going to answer that?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Er, well, no. It's stopped now anyway.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
...where Anna is behaving strangely.
(ringing starts again)

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I gave you a long lesson on how to answer the phone and you're still too scared!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text:
It's not that.
(desk phone starts ringing)

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: For goodness sake!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Then what?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I recognise the number - it's Mr Lime!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Ha! Old Slimy Limy, he must be absolutely desperate to get you to have lunch with him – even after your cruel rejection. Here, I'll answer for you.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I'll answer. Hello, Tip Top Trading, Anna's phone... no, this is Denise speaking, Anna's busy at the moment. Can I take a message?... Yes... right.... I'll pass that on to her then… thank you for calling. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Nothing about lunch. He wants each Imperial Lemon you deliver to come in a luxury green box – like the one you had at the presentation.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: My goodness, we don't have many in stock, I'll have to order some. Erm...(dials a number) Hello, this is Anna speaking from Tip Top Trading, I want some imperial lemon-sized luxury boxes.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Woah, woah, woah.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Let's make this order a bit more politely okay?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Why are the English so obsessed with being polite!?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Calm down Anna and listen to me. To put in an order for something, you need phrases like:
I'd like to place an order for...
We're going to need...
Could you send...
Could we also have...
When can we expect to receive them?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right... Hello, sorry about that... I'd like to place an order for some imperial lemon-sized luxury boxes, please... we're going to need quite a few... could you send 300 please... yes... the green ones... could we also have the name of our company on the sides... when can we expect to receive them...okay, thank you, goodbye. There! How was that?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Good, well done!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: You'd better phone back Mr Lime to confirm he can have his boxes!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh no!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: He's your client!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yes Anna, he's your client!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'm scared he'll try and ask about lunch again.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Then send him an email.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Good idea!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Copy in me, Tom and Paul, so it’s clear you only mean business only.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes. Thanks Denise! An email is much safer.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
Is it, Anna, is it? Hmmm...
Anyway, here are the phrases Anna used to place her order:
Let's see if Anna's email is really such a good idea. I have a bad feeling about it. Until next time!
